issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that local optimality of sparse solutions lets the exact and robust recovery theories of other penalties carry over to the TH models. What is proved (Theorem TH:s-sparse) is only that any feasible s-sparse vector whose nonzero entries exceed mu is a local minimizer; the same argument makes essentially every feasible vector with all entries above mu a local minimizer, so no uniqueness, global-optimality, noise-robust error bound, or exact-recovery statement follows. No recovery theorem for Phi_mu is stated or proved anywhere, and the paper's own failure analysis reports "model failures", i.e., instances where the ground truth is not the model's global minimizer, which is exactly the failure of exact recovery at the model level.

failure_location.quote: This property allows the exact and robust recovery theories developed for other penalty regularization functions to be directly extended to the truncated Huber function.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the abstract (and the matching introduction sentence) to the proved statement, namely local optimality of s-sparse feasible vectors with entries above mu, and drop the promise that exact/robust recovery theories extend; supporting that promise would require new global recovery theorems for Phi_mu.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised direct transfer of exact and robust recovery guarantees to the truncated Huber penalty is unsupported; the paper establishes only local minimality of sparse feasible vectors and no exact-recovery, uniqueness, or robust error bound for (constrain_model) or (obj_singleu).
issues.title: Abstract claims exact/robust recovery theories transfer directly to TH
issues.why_classification: The advertised recovery guarantee cannot be kept without new recovery theory, so the promise must be withdrawn; this is a limited weakening of the prose that leaves every proved result intact, hence more than a routine local fix but no major loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that $\mathrm{spark}(A)=m+1$ and the initial value $\cQ_\mu(\wvx^0,\widehat\vomega^0)< \mathrm{spark}(A)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The updates (updateforx_I1) and (formulation_y) invert A_{I_2^j}A_{I_2^j}^T, which needs rank(A_{I_2^j}) = m, i.e. card(I_2^j) >= m. The text justifies this with "card(I_2^j) >= (n-m) > m", but n > 2m is not among the hypotheses (spark(A) = m+1 and Q_mu(x0,omega0) < spark(A)); only card(I_1^j) <= m is proved. E.g. m = 2, n = 3, A = [[1,0,1],[0,1,1]] (spark = 3), b = (1,1), mu = 1/2, x0 = (1,1,0), omega0 = (1,1,0) (Q_mu = 2 < spark(A)) give I_1 = {1,2}, I_2 = {3}, and A_{I_2}A_{I_2}^T = [[1,1],[1,1]] is singular, so the x-update is not defined although every stated hypothesis holds.

failure_location.quote: the matrices $A_{\cI^{j}_{1}}^\top A_{\cI^{j}_{1}}$ and $A_{\cI^{j}_{2}}A_{\cI^{j}_{2}}^\top$ are invertible.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis n >= 2m (equivalently card(I_2^j) >= m) to the noise-free scheme and to Theorem covgergalg1, or replace (A_{I_2}A_{I_2}^T)^{-1} by a pseudoinverse/least-squares update and re-derive the formulas.
issues.overall_effect: The noise-free branch of Algorithm BCD (its x-update) is undefined whenever card(I_2^j) < m, so the iterates to which Theorem covgergalg1 refers may not exist and the theorem is unsupported on its stated hypothesis set.
issues.title: Noise-free BCD update undefined unless card(I_2^j) >= m
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard hypothesis n >= 2m leaves the update formulas, the finite-step convergence conclusion, and the advertised under-determined regime m << n unchanged, so the least repair is a local condition rather than a new construction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Theorem  \ref{linearoptcond} establishes that $(\wvx, \widehat{\vomega})$ is a minimizer of the model \eqref{constrain_model}.
then $\wvx$ is a local minimizer of $\min_{\vx\in\cS} \Phi_{\mu}(\vx)$.
Then, the sequence $\{(\wvx^k,\widehat\vomega^k)\}_k$ is bounded and converges to the minimizer of model \eqref{obj_singleu} in a finite number of steps.

issues.failure_explanation: The statements claim convergence to "the minimizer" of the non-convex models, i.e. to a global minimizer. The proofs only invoke the "local or global minimizer" characterizations of Theorems linearoptcond and noise_optcond and conclude at most that the limit is "a minimizer", i.e. a local one; no global-optimality argument is given and Theorem TH:s-sparse shows the models have many local minimizers. The global claim is false: for A = [1,2] (spark(A) = 2 = m+1), b = 2, mu = 1, x0 = (2,0), omega0 = (1,0) (Q_mu = 1 < spark(A)) the noise-free iterates stay at ((2,0),(1,0)), while the feasible point (0.4,0.8) has Phi_mu = 0.8 < 1 = Phi_mu(2,0) on the same constraint x_1+2x_2 = 2.

failure_location.quote: Then, the sequence $\{(\wvx^{k},\widehat{\vomega}^{k})\}_k$ is bounded and converges to the minimizer of model \eqref{constrain_model} in a finite number of steps.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace "the minimizer" by "a local minimizer" in both statements so that the claims match the local optimality the proofs target.
issues.overall_effect: Theorems covgergalg1 and convergalg2 advertise convergence of Algorithm BCD to the model's minimizer (a global solution); only convergence to a local minimizer is ever established, so any global-optimality guarantee for the algorithm is unsupported.
issues.title: Convergence statements claim 'the minimizer' but only local optimality is in reach
issues.why_classification: The repair is a limited weakening that keeps the finite-step convergence and everything the proofs establish, but it necessarily withdraws the global-optimality guarantee asserted in the statements, so it exceeds a repair that preserves the claim as made.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: A vector $\widehat{\vx}$ minimizes \eqref{constrain_model} locally or globally if and only if $\abs{\wvx_i}\neq \mu$ for all $i$ and there exists $\wvy\in\rr^m$ such that
A vector $\widehat{\vx}$ is a local or global minimizer of \eqref{obj_singleu}  if and only if $\abs{\wvx_i}\neq \mu$ for all $i$, and there exists $\widehat{\vomega}\in\rr^n$ such that
According to Theorem \ref{noise_optcond}, the limit point $(\wvx,\widehat{\vomega})$ is a minimizer of model \eqref{obj_singleu}.

issues.failure_explanation: Both optimality characterizations require |x_i| != mu for every i, but the fixed-point equations the limit satisfies do not enforce this: they give only (2/mu^2)(1-omega) composed with x_bar + A^T y = 0 with omega = H_mu(x_bar), and H_mu returns 0 at |x_bar_i| = mu. Such a limit need not be a local minimizer. Counterexample (noise-free): A = [1,2] (spark = 2 = m+1), b = 2.5, mu = 1, x0 = (0.5,1), omega0 = (0,0) (Q_mu = 1.25 < spark(A)). The x-update returns the minimum-norm solution (0.5,1) and the omega-update returns H_1((0.5,1)) = (0,0) because |1| <= mu, so the iterates are constant. Yet along the feasible direction v = (-2,1), Phi_mu((0.5,1)+t v) = (0.5-2t)^2 + 1 < 1.25 = Phi_mu((0.5,1)) for 0 < t < 1/2, so (0.5,1) is not a local minimizer. The same failure occurs in the noisy model.

failure_location.quote: Theorem  \ref{linearoptcond} establishes that $(\wvx, \widehat{\vomega})$ is a minimizer of the model \eqref{constrain_model}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the conclusions to finite-step convergence to a fixed point of the BCD that is a local minimizer whenever |x_bar_i| != mu for all i, or prove/assume avoidance of the kink set and re-run the optimality argument.
issues.overall_effect: The conclusions of Theorems covgergalg1 and convergalg2 that the iterates converge to a minimizer are false: the finite-step limit can be a kink fixed point with |x_bar_i| = mu that is not a local minimizer; at best the argument yields a fixed point that is a local minimizer when the limit avoids the values +/- mu.
issues.title: BCD limit at a kink |x_i| = mu need not be a local minimizer
issues.why_classification: Finite-step convergence survives and the failure is confined to fixed points on the degenerate set {|x_bar_i| = mu}, so a limited weakening plus a short case argument restores a recognizably comparable result; no new global proof architecture is needed, but "converges to a minimizer" cannot stand as written.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: From Lemma \ref{mudecre_objincre} and Lemma \ref{upperbound_lema2_rev}, we can easily obtain

issues.failure_explanation: The denominator m - n + card(K+1) equals m - #{i : |(x_k)_i| > c_{k+1}} and is negative as soon as more than n - m entries exceed c_{k+1} = mu_k/rho (and is zero at equality), so the square root is not a real number although the spark bound is maintained. E.g. m = 2, n = 10, rho = 2, mu_k = 1, x_k = (0.6,0.6,0.6,0.1,0,...,0) has #{|x_i| > mu_k} = 0 <= m and Q_mu(x_k,H(x_k)) = 1.09 < spark(A) = 3, but card(K+1) = 7 gives denominator 2 - 10 + 7 = -1 with numerator 0.01 > 0. Moreover, the two cited lemmas give only monotonicity of the optimal value in mu and min_omega Q = Phi; neither yields this rule nor proves that it preserves the invertibility/level bound it is introduced for, and the sum over K+1 omits entries with c_{k+1} < |x_i| <= mu_{k+1} that also enter Phi_{mu_{k+1}}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-derive the update from the requirement Q_{mu_{k+1}}(x_k, H_{mu_{k+1}}(x_k)) < spark(A) (which yields a threshold with denominator m+1-n+card(K) over the full small-entry set K), and specify a fallback when that bound is unavailable.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm continuescheme cannot compute mu_{k+1} on such iterates, so the continuation strategy and with it the claimed safeguard of matrix invertibility are undefined in a regime the paper says the strategy is designed to handle; even where defined, the level/invertibility bound it is meant to enforce is unproved.
issues.title: Continuation rule for mu is ill-defined (negative radicand, zero denominator)
issues.why_classification: A complete repair needs a re-derivation of the rule and an argument that the new mu preserves the level/invertibility bound, i.e. a contained but nontrivial construction plus reoptimization of the parameter choice; the formula cannot be kept with a purely local correction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For the DCT matrix $A_2 \in \mathbb{R}^{64 \times 1024}$ ($F = 5$, $s = 8$), the $TH$ method again outperforms all other methods, especially in low-noise conditions.
Although the $L_0$ model exhibits competitive performance at higher noise levels, its effectiveness does not improve significantly as the noise decreases.

issues.failure_explanation: The conclusion asserts that TH has the lowest RRE at every SNR level. In the reported DCT experiment (SNR 30 dB row of the table whose columns are SNR, L1, TL1, L1L2, L0, MCP, Lp, TH) the L0 method has a lower mean RRE than TH (0.4138 versus 0.4270), so the claim is contradicted by the paper's own data; the section text "again outperforms all other methods" carries the same defect at high noise.

failure_location.quote: For noisy observations, it maintains the lowest RRE the entire range of SNR levels.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to the range in which TH is actually best, e.g. "lowest RRE at all SNR levels except the highest-noise setting of the DCT experiment", and align the corresponding sentence in Section 4.4.
issues.overall_effect: The conclusion's robustness claim over the full SNR range is overstated; the data support only "lowest RRE at all SNR levels except the highest-noise setting of the DCT experiment".
issues.title: Conclusion claims lowest RRE over the whole SNR range, contradicted by the data
issues.why_classification: A one-clause correction of an empirical summary keeps every other claim, method, and guarantee intact, with no new argument or construction required.
